newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Trelleborg stock up on Boliden sale.
newsitem.headline: Trelleborg stock up on Boliden sale.

text.p: Shares in metals and mining group Trelleborg AB rose on Thursday amid speculation how much the company would gain from spinning off its Boliden unit.
Trelleborg's B share was traded 5.50 crowns higher at 137.50 crowns at 0940 GMT on the Stockholm stock exchange.
Trelleborg has said it applied to Canadian regulatory authorities to list its mining unit Boliden Ltd in Canada and that it would retain between 45 and 49 percent of Boliden after the listing.
"The share is rising because it is time for Trelleborg's road shows and because (Swedish brokerage) Carnegie has issued a positive analysis," one dealer said.
Financial daily Dagens Industri on Thursday quoted sources in Toronto as saying that Trelleborg was expected to get close to Canadian $900 million for the 51 percent Trelleborg plans to sell.
Dagens Industri also said that Carnegie in its latest analysis estimated Boliden's value at around eight billion crowns.
Carnegie valued the Trelleborg share at between 175 and 225 crowns after the spinoff of Boliden.
Carnegie analyst Christofer Sjogren said the analysis was written at the end of March.
"We have different price intervals depending on what Trelleborg does with the money from Boliden. Dagens Industri has just picked one of them," he said.
